correctness.rationale: Legendre's three-square criterion reduces the obstruction to an even 2-adic valuation and odd unit 7 mod 8. The factor-exponent identity separates odd and even indices, yielding the proven binary formulas. Exact integer matrix checks of a complete 32-state transition table certify row and column sums 2, strong connectivity, a self-loop and the degree-18 annihilator. Its nontrivial roots have modulus sqrt(2), yielding a square-root discrepancy. The all-j exact dyadic formula follows from checking 34 specified output terms and the Cayley-Hamilton theorem for a 34-dimensional block diagonal operator. The supplied verifier runs from the embedded artifact and also independently checks 4097 successive odd-part and valuation cases. No infinite conclusion relies solely on sampling.

originality.rationale: The exact object is the product of consecutive factorials, not the individual factorials classified in Burns 2021 and 2022. The latter work does imply the density and order of the error upon combination with the proven even-index reduction; the claim of new contribution therefore rests on the specific all-index binary characterization and exact dyadic fluctuation, neither stated by the inspected primary results. Aliyev 2022 determines valuations only. No covering exact theorem was found in the inspected literature or records.

value.rationale: Superfactorials are naturally defined Barnes-G integer values and consecutive Vandermonde determinants. Legendre three-square representability is a natural invariant motivated by existing factorial work. The theorem gives a complete explicit binary characterization and an exact infinite fluctuation that makes the square-root exponent optimal, an invariant not determined by the previously known density. It is not a finite arbitrary sample or a renaming of ordinary-factorial statements.
